subject: Physics
chapter: Chapter 2: Motion in a Straight Line
central_question: How can position, velocity, acceleration, and relative motion along a straight line be described and predicted?
in_scope_units: Introduction to rectilinear motion, point-object approximation, origin, position, and displacement.
Instantaneous velocity and speed as limiting rates and graph slopes.
Average and instantaneous acceleration and velocity–time graphs.
Kinematic equations for constant acceleration, free fall, stopping distance, and reaction time.

known_pitfalls.claim: Negative acceleration always means slowing down.
known_pitfalls.correction: Speed decreases only when acceleration is opposite to velocity.
At a turning point velocity may be zero while acceleration remains non-zero.

known_pitfalls.claim: Average speed equals magnitude of average velocity.
known_pitfalls.correction: Average speed is greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Kinematic equations apply to every motion.
known_pitfalls.correction: The standard equations require constant acceleration.

known_pitfalls.claim: Area under a speed–time graph is signed displacement.
known_pitfalls.correction: Signed area under a velocity–time graph gives displacement.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Example 2.1: differentiate x = a + bt².
NCERT Example 2.3: vertical throw from a 25.0 m building.
